items.failureInterpretation: Lock timeout not observed on the redemption-first test means redemption never held auth-inviter:<user> through the user insert, or the gate trigger did not run. A redemption that succeeds after the offboarding commit means the re-read or the same-statement revoke did not happen. A sibling that stays unrevoked after the later suspend means the trigger did not update pending invites. A 500ms lock-wait failure means the second offboarding did not block.

items.failureInterpretation: A forbidden result that throws instead of returning means the authority load aborted the transaction. Platform 0013 must already be installed, and app.current_user_id must be set before the decision. An administrator place that returns ok means the administrator role is still treated as authority. A ceremony failure before any hold means the issuance rules, membership capacities, or platform 0029 and 0030 were not loaded. An injected audit fault that leaves a hold_release row or a second live retention row means the write committed without its audit. A member who can see the hold reference, or an administrator who can read the thread after the recorded hold, means the privacy boundary failed.
items.recovery: Drop the disposable database. Apply 0029 and 0030 through the platform journal executor. Do not edit 0013. Do not grant a hold or a retention power by inserting a mandate outside the issuance workflow.
